Jet pT-Response Regression — Tier 0+1 Report

ATLAS/HEP presentation. Isolated test jets unless noted; error bars are statistical (median: 1.253σrob/√n; JER: 1.16·JER/√n; histograms: √N). "Network" curves use seed 0; the summary table averages 3 seeds.

1. What was done

4 of 17 5D ttbar files → 146k truth-matched light jets (pt_true > 20 GeV, recomputed ΔR < 0.3, |η| < 2.5; isolation stored as a flag - D1). Per jet: target y = ln(pt_true/pt_reco) (D2), 6 jet features, ghost tracks ×18, cone cells ×7 with the calo neighbor subgraph via exact cell matching (0 unmatched cells). Training: isolated jets, flat-pT weights, Huber→Gaussian NLL, 3 seeds × 4 configs on 4×A30. Tier-0 gate passed (test response median 1.065).

2. Dataset diagnostics

3. How the metrics are computed

Corrected response per jet: rcorr = (pt_reco/pt_true)·eμ. Per bin: JES = median(rcorr); JER = (q75−q25)/1.349 ÷ median; pull = (y−μ)/σ.

5. D1: the isolation gap

6. Findings

F1: the calo neighbor graph beats set encoding on every metric (C2 answered) - topology is a real inductive bias even at ~30 cells/jet.
F2: constituents carry the resolution (~30% JER gain); the jet 4-vector alone carries none (J = B0 resolution). Cells win at high pT.
F3: the isolation gap is real and measured - Stage-2's target.
P1: closure misses 1-2% via the universal 20-30 GeV bin + a ~2% NLL estimator offset; MAE variant / numerical inversion queued for Tier 2.
